Run the examples below or browse the [Shiny gallery](shiny-gallery.html){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.
Each app has its own folder under [`pkgdown/shiny/` on GitHub](https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter/tree/main/pkgdown/shiny).
The first launch downloads R and its dependencies. The apps use the highcharter version documented here.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(htmltools)
demo <- function(slug, title, height = 450) {
  url <- paste0("../live/", slug, "/index.html")
  source_url <- paste0(
    "https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter/blob/main/pkgdown/shiny/",
    slug,
    "/app.R"
  )
  tagList(
    tags$div(
      class = "shiny-app-frame",
      tags$iframe(
        title = title,
        src = url,
        class = paste0("shiny-app-", slug),
        loading = "lazy",
        width = "100%",
        height = height,
        style = "border:0"
      )
    ),
    tags$p(
      tags$a(
        href = url,
        "Open the app in its own tab",
        target = "_blank",
        rel = "noopener"
      ),
      " · ",
      tags$a(href = source_url, "View app.R on GitHub")
    )
  )
}
```

## Basics

Select **Sepal** or **Petal**. The same 150 flowers move to their new coordinates.
Put `highchartOutput("flowers")` in the UI and read `input$measure` inside
`renderHighchart()` to rebuild the plot when the measurement changes.

```{r basic, echo=FALSE}
demo("basic", "the iris explorer")
```

## Proxies

The [original proxy playground](https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter-shiny/tree/master/02-proxy-functions)
inspired these three examples. Each tab creates its chart once, then uses
`highchartProxy()` to change the chart already on screen.

* **Series.** Compare monthly temperatures in Santiago and Tokyo. Toggle Tokyo
  to add or remove its series. Switch from daily means to daily highs to
  replace the data by series ID with `hcpxy_set_data()`. A single
  `hcpxy_redraw()` displays both changes. Try the same comparison on polar axes.
* **Points.** Add or remove a month of observed air traffic. Turn on the
  dashed forecast to repeat the last twelve observations one year ahead.
  The forecast moves with the observations, even when you switch to columns.
* **Layout.** Rearrange the same 592 students into a grid, semicircle or circle.
  `hcpxy_update_series()` changes the item layout while preserving the counts.

```{r proxy, echo=FALSE}
demo("proxy", "the proxy playground", height = 510)
```

To switch from weekly to daily Stock prices when the visible date range narrows, [run the Stock proxy app](../live/stock/index.html) or
[read the Stock walkthrough](stock.html#update-a-series-and-its-visible-range-in-shiny).

## Events

Gain ranges from −12 dB (cut) to +12 dB (boost), with 0 dB neutral.
Hover over a band, click it, then drag the arrow at its top and release it. Each event has
its own readout. The `drag` and `mouseOver` values refresh at most once every
150 ms. The `drop` value shows the final gain as soon as you release the band.

```{r events, echo=FALSE}
demo("events", "the equalizer", height = 595)
```

Point clicks arrive automatically at `input$eq_point_click`. Register
`mouseOver`, `drag` and `drop` with `hc_add_event_point()` to receive their
inputs too. For example, `input$eq_point_mouseOver$pointid` identifies the
band under the pointer and `input$eq_point_drag$y` gives its gain during a drag.

## Linked views

The dotplot shows mean petal length by species, rounded to the nearest
millimeter. With `colorByPoint = TRUE`, each species gets its own color.
Pause over a species for 200 ms or click it for an immediate selection. The
detail shows petal length and width for its 50 flowers in the same color.
A Shiny proxy animates the 50 dots to the new species' measurements and
updates the color and title. The axes stay fixed for comparison.

```{r linked, echo=FALSE}
demo("linked", "the linked charts", height = 400)
```

To run an example from a local checkout, load the package and open the app directory:

```{r local-app, eval=FALSE}
pkgload::load_all()
shiny::runApp("pkgdown/shiny/events")
```

The [original Shiny examples](https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter-shiny)
also include a [population explorer with linked views](https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter-shiny/tree/master/08-idb-viz).
